title: assure record
description: --commit is the full commit that is checked out. The two suite flags name the results of the two test suites. --predicate names the file to write; it must be outside the checkout. Writes the proof run predicate for the provider to attest, and prints the count of outcomes by result, and the predicate's path, digest, type and signer. Exits 0 when it writes the predicate. Exits 1, and writes nothing, on an unknown or malformed test ID, a commit that is not the full commit checked out, a tree with changes that are not committed, or a job that is not the trusted signer. Exits 2 when a flag is missing or another argument is given.

title: assure gate change
description: --commit is the full commit of the change. --base is the full commit at the head of the branch that the change merges into. The optional tool flag names the specification tool to use, if not the one of the checkout. Prints the decision with every reason. Exits 0 when the change passes and 1 when it is refused. Exits 2, with no decision, when it is called wrongly or cannot decide, such as when the specification has an error at either commit; it then says that no decision was reached, and why.

title: assure gate release
description: --commit is the full commit to release. --predicate names the file for the decision predicate; it must be outside the checkout, and no file may be there already. The optional tool flag names the specification tool to use, if not the one of the checkout. Prints the decision with every reason. After a refused decision it prints one notice line, release refused: N reasons. Writes the decision predicate only when the release passes. Exits 0 when the release passes and 1 when it is refused; a refused release is a neutral outcome of the run. Exits 2, with no predicate, when it is called wrongly, when its output place is refused, or when it cannot decide, such as when the specification has an error at the commit or the job is not the trusted release job at main; it then says that no decision was reached, and why.

title: assure ledger
description: --commit is the full commit to show. --depth is the maximum number of commits of first-parent history to walk from it, 200 by default. Prints the proof ledger: one line per test record in ID order with its state, its result at the commit (passed, failed, skipped or none) and the last commit a verified proof run passed it at, or not within the commits walked; then the release-grade proof run at the commit with its signer and log entry, or why there is none; then each change-grade attestation at a commit walked, which counts only in its own gate; then each attestation that was refused, with the reason; then the test records that did not pass. Only a release-grade proof run gives results and last passes. The walk stops when every automated test record has passed somewhere. Exits 0 when a release-grade proof run at the commit passed every automated test record, and 1 when one did not or there is no such proof run. Exits 2, with no ledger, when it is called wrongly or the ledger cannot be built, such as when the commit has no specification or the provider's store cannot answer.

title: stego deps
description: Takes no flag and no argument. Resolves the service's modules, writes the module list and its checksums, and prints that they are resolved and must be committed with the application changes.

title: stego build download
description: --source is the source location and --revision its full commit ID. --module is the module path in the source, the top by default. --target is the path of the program to build, in the module. --go is the Go tool of the selected official SDK. --output is a new folder for the module cache. Writes the module cache that the revision needs, with its cache record. All flags but --module are required.

title: stego build
description: --source is the source location and --revision its full commit ID. --module is the module path in the source, the top by default. --target is the path of the program to build, in the module. --go is the Go tool of the selected official SDK, given as a flag, not taken from the archetype. --work is a new private build folder and --output a new result folder. --module-cache is the module cache that stego build download recorded for the revision; it is required, since a build runs offline and never downloads modules, and a build without it is refused before any work. Writes the executable, its build record and both SBOMs into the result folder. Prints the Application built event as one line of JSON: the revision, the digest of the build record and the digest of the executable.

title: stego image build
description: --build-record is the verified build record and --build-record-sha256 its trusted digest. --application is the executable. --trust-store is the explicit CA bundle and --trust-store-sha256 its trusted digest. --entrypoint is the name of the executable in the image, application by default. --output is a new private result folder. In place of the three, --after is a file that holds the Application built event that stego build printed, and --build-result the result folder of that build: the image is then built from the build record there at the digest the event names, and from the executable that record names only, and a build record or an executable given beside the event is refused. Writes the image and its image record into the result folder, and prints the Image built event as one line of JSON: the image digest and the build record digest.

title: stego image sign
description: --image is the folder that stego image build wrote, with the image record, the build record and both SBOMs, and --record-sha256 the trusted digest of the image record. In place of --record-sha256, --after is a file that holds the Image built event that stego image build printed: the image record in the folder is then read at the digest of its bytes and refused unless it names the image and the build record the event names. --spdx-bundle and --cyclonedx-bundle are the provider's signature bundles of the SPDX and the CycloneDX SBOM attestations about the image digest. --signer-issuer and --signer-subject name the trusted signer: the issuer that vouched for it and the pipeline definition it ran as, at its exact reference. --gh is the absolute path of the provider's program that verifies the bundles, and --source-repository the repository of the signed run, as owner/name. Every flag is required, and a missing flag is refused by name before any file is read or any connection opens. Checks the image against its record, and that the provider's trusted signer signed both SBOMs of its build record about the image digest; then writes the signature record in the image folder, prints the signature references, and prints the Image signed event as one line of JSON: the image digest and the signer. Exits non-zero with the reason, and writes nothing, when a check fails.

title: stego image publish
description: --record is the image record and --record-sha256 its trusted digest. --image is the folder of the image to publish and --build-record its build record. The registry flags name the explicit place of the image in the registry, with no tag; --registry-ca, the registry's CA bundle; and --registry-ca-sha256, its trusted digest. --credentials is a private file with the user name and password. --token-origin and --blob-origin each name one approved secure origin, once per origin. --work is a new private result folder. In place of --record, --record-sha256 and --build-record, --after is a file that holds the Image signed event that stego image sign printed, and --image is then the image folder that stego image sign signed: the signature record there must be of the image and the signer the event names, and the signature flags, as stego image sign takes them, must check it again before anything is pushed; an image with no signature record is refused. The signature flags, as stego image sign takes them, are required on both ways: a missing flag is refused by name before any file is read, any credential is opened or any connection opens, and the image is pushed only when its signature by the trusted signer verifies. Pushes the image, reads it back, writes the image record of what the registry holds into the result folder, and prints the Image published event as one line of JSON: the image digest and the repository.

title: stego build verify
description: --record is the build record, --record-sha256 its digest from verified provenance, and --artifact the executable. All three are required. Checks the executable against the trusted record, and exits non-zero with the reason when it does not match.

title: stego build verify-source
description: --record is the build record, --record-sha256 its digest from verified provenance, and --source a complete source snapshot with no version control data or build caches. All three are required. Checks the snapshot against the trusted record's source inventory, and exits non-zero with the reason when it does not match.

title: stego image verify
description: --record is the image record and --record-sha256 its trusted digest. --image is the local image folder and --build-record its build record. --work is a new private folder for the check. --spdx-bundle and --cyclonedx-bundle are the provider's signature bundles of the SPDX and the CycloneDX SBOM attestations about the image digest. --signer-issuer and --signer-subject name the trusted signer: the issuer that vouched for it and the pipeline definition it ran as, at its exact reference. --gh is the absolute path of the provider's program that verifies the bundles, and --source-repository the repository of the signed run, as owner/name. Every flag is required, and a missing flag is refused by name before any file is read or any connection opens. Checks the local image against its record, its trusted build record and its signature by the trusted signer, and exits non-zero with the reason when any of the three does not match.

title: stego image retrieve
description: --record is the image record and --record-sha256 its trusted digest. --build-record is the trusted build record. The registry flags name the explicit place of the image in the registry, with no tag; --registry-ca, the registry's CA bundle; and --registry-ca-sha256, its trusted digest. --credentials is a private file with the user name and password. --token-origin and --blob-origin each name one approved secure origin, once per origin. --work is a new private result folder. --spdx-bundle and --cyclonedx-bundle are the provider's signature bundles of the SPDX and the CycloneDX SBOM attestations about the image digest. --signer-issuer and --signer-subject name the trusted signer: the issuer that vouched for it and the pipeline definition it ran as, at its exact reference. --gh is the absolute path of the provider's program that verifies the bundles, and --source-repository the repository of the signed run, as owner/name. Every flag is required, and a missing flag is refused by name before any file is read or any connection opens. Pulls the image, checks it against its record, its trusted build record and its signature, and only then writes it into the result folder. Exits non-zero, writes the image nowhere, and names the check or input, when a check fails or an input is refused before any connection.

title: stego image export
description: --record is the image record and --record-sha256 its trusted digest. --image is the local image folder and --build-record its build record. --work is a new private result folder. Checks the image against its record and its trusted build record, writes it as image.docker.tar, an archive that a container engine can load, with export.json, and exits non-zero with the reason when it does not match.

title: stego init
description: --archetype names the archetype and is required; no other argument is taken. Writes a new declaration in the current folder with the smallest example content that checking accepts, and a folder for fills, and prints the project name and each file it created.

title: stego validate
description: Takes one optional flag. Checks the declaration and prints every fault, or that there is none. Without a flag it prints each fault for a person, rendered from the structured fault: the rule, the path, the message, the value found and the allowed values. With --json it prints only one JSON document on standard output, which holds accepted and the faults in the order the check found them, each with the rule, the path, the value found, the allowed values and the message, and for a declaration that cannot be read as one document the line and the position in the line. With the faults, prints each pin of the service with its standing: superseded with its successor and fail date, withdrawn with its fail date, or unchecked when the lifecycle records cannot be read. Exits non-zero when there is a fault, or a pin that is withdrawn or past its fail date, and not for a pin that is only superseded. stego plan and stego apply print the same standing before they go on.

title: stego lifecycle supersede
description: --registry is the registry checkout whose lifecycle folder gets the advisory. --component names the component, or --runtime the module path of the runtime library. --digest is the superseded component digest or runtime version, and --successor the digest that replaces it; --successor-component names the successor's component when it is another component that took over the port. --fails-after is the last day on which a pin to the superseded digest stands. --needs-declaration-change and --needs-fill-change state yes or no. --summary says what the successor changes, in one line. --reference is a link to the change, its review or its release notes, and may repeat. It records one OSV advisory and prints its id.

title: stego lifecycle withdraw
description: --registry is the registry checkout whose lifecycle folder gets the advisory. --component names the component, or --runtime the module path of the runtime library. --digest is the withdrawn component digest or runtime version. --fails-after is the future day after which a pin that a service already holds fails; a date already past is refused. --reason says why the digest must not be used. --reference is a link to the finding, and may repeat. It records one OSV advisory and prints its id.

title: qualify-compiler-release.py
description: A release script, not a stego command. --revision is the full lower-case commit ID to qualify. --output is a new result folder whose parent exists. --gh is the absolute path of the hosted CI provider's installed client. Writes the qualification record of the commit into the result folder and prints it.

title: qualify-compiler-release.py --verify-release
description: A release script, not a stego command. --verify-release verifies the release that is already published, as a consumer installs it, in place of a candidate. --revision is the full lower-case commit ID of the release. --output is a new result folder whose parent exists. --gh is the absolute path of the hosted CI provider's installed client. Writes the qualification record, with the verified release, into the result folder and prints it.

title: install-compiler.py
description: An installation script, not a stego command. --revision is the full lower-case commit ID of the release. --output is a new result folder whose parent exists. --gh is the absolute path of the hosted CI provider's installed client. Give --release to download the published release, or --package to install from a folder that holds the release assets. Installs one verified release on Linux amd64: writes the compiler and its build record into the result folder and prints the verified record.

title: stego fleet
description: --digest is the component digest. Each <checkout> is a service checkout to read. Prints every recorded service that pins the digest, with the version and digest it holds, and each checkout without a readable record as unknown.

title: stego version
description: Prints the version; with its one flag it prints the version and the build identity as structured output.

title: stego fleet measures
description: Each <checkout> is a service checkout to read. Sweeps the checkouts once and prints each outcome measure with the services behind it, and for each service each default it left and each public operation with the reason from its committed record, as text, or with its one flag as structured output.

title: stego fleet vex
description: --registry is the registry checkout whose lifecycle folder holds the advisories. Each <checkout> is a service checkout to read. Sweeps the checkouts once and prints one OpenVEX document with one statement per service and advisory. It writes nothing.

title: stego delivery check
description: --image is the image that the CI provider built, by reference and digest. --record is its build record and --record-sha256 the record's trusted digest. --policy is the delivery policy file that the pipeline carries and --policy-sha256 that file's trusted digest, which the CI file passes. Refuses a record or a policy file whose SHA-256 digest is not the trusted digest, before any check. Runs every STEGO check on the image as the last step of each provider's pipeline, evaluates the policy file it was given, prints each check with its result and the policy file it evaluated, and exits non-zero when any check fails.

title: stego env check
description: --requirements is the service's platform requirements file and <environment-file> the environment to check. Prints every platform requirement that the environment does not meet, and exits non-zero when one is unmet.

title: stego fill create
description: <name> is the new fill's name. --slot is the slot it fills and is required. --component names the component that owns the slot, when more than one component declares a slot of that name. --collection is the collection the fill is for. Writes the fill and its code in the fills folder, and prints each file it created and what to do next.

title: stego test
description: Takes no flag of its own. Runs the tests of every fill and prints their results. Arguments after -- go to the test run. Exits non-zero when a test fails.

title: stego fill sign
description: <name> is the fill to sign off. Signs the fill's current evidence with the person's key, writes the sign-off into the fill's record, and prints it.

title: stego fill status
description: Takes no flag. Prints each fill that the declaration binds, with its qualification and fit.

title: stego fill upgrade
description: Takes no flag. Removes qualified_by and qualified_at from each fill manifest under fills/, prints each fill it changed and the next steps stego test and stego fill sign, and prints that nothing changed when no manifest holds them. Exits non-zero, and changes no manifest, when one cannot be read.

title: stego apply
description: --replace-hand-edits lets the run replace generated files that were edited by hand; without it, apply names every generated file that is missing or no longer matches its recorded hash, and writes nothing. --saved-plan carries out the plan that stego plan saved, and refuses it, writing nothing, when a plan made now gives another; every apply removes the saved plan. Makes a plan, writes its files and the new record, and prints the plan and that the apply is complete; when the plan changes nothing it prints that and writes nothing. With the generated code, one apply writes the architecture view and the architecture model file; the platform requirements file, from the declaration and its components' needs; the service's CI file for the provider that the delivery stanza names, with the pinned references and trusted signer from the registry; the service's deployment base, which plain kustomize builds, and the offline Containerfile; and the delivery object from the delivery stanza. The plan lists each of these files. When the declaration has no delivery stanza, it writes no delivery object and says so in the plan. It writes nothing, and names the cause, when a component states no architecture role; when a need holds an environment value or two components state one need with different shapes; when the CI file was edited by hand, the declaration sets a pipeline reference or signer, or a reference is not pinned; or when the delivery stanza names a destination, a namespace or an overlay. --base names the commit or branch of the version that runs now, and the repository's default branch is the default; apply writes nothing, and names each fault, when the check against it (ST-GEN-QRY04) finds a fault. Before it plans, apply writes into the declaration an add step for each new entity and each new optional field of an entity of the base that no step declares, and names each one, so the author commits them.

title: stego recover
description: Takes no flag and no argument. Completes an interrupted apply, and prints that no pending apply remains.

title: stego plan
description: Makes a plan, saves it in STEGO's working state in the service, and prints the action for each generated file: each file that the plan would create, update or delete, and whether the record changes. It writes no generated file and does not change the record. With --show it saves no plan, and prints the saved plan and whether it still applies. stego apply --saved-plan carries out the saved plan. --base names the commit or branch of the version that runs now, and the repository's default branch is the default; plan saves no plan, and names each fault, when the check against it (ST-GEN-QRY04) finds a fault. The plan lists each new schema step with its change, kind, phase, migration, trigger and backfill.

title: stego assets
description: --directory is the frontend build folder, with its index file and assets. --output is the bundle file to write. Both are required. Checks every entry and writes a checked asset bundle.

title: stego fix
description: Rewrites the declaration to the next declaration version that the registry accepts, and prints each construct it cannot rewrite, with its path. With --dry-run it prints the rewrite and writes nothing.

title: stego drift
description: Takes no flag. Prints every drifted generated file and recorded input, and exits non-zero when there is any.

title: stego compat
description: --base names the commit or branch of the version that runs now, and is required; in the change gate it is the pull request's base. Reads the declaration and the record at that ref from the service's repository. Prints the base ref and its commit, and each fault against the base with its entity, field, rule and the schema change and phase to declare; --json prints them as one JSON object. Exits 0 with no fault, 1 with a fault, and 2 for a usage error or a ref that it cannot read.

title: stego registry promote
description: <component> is the component in the local registry. --to is a checkout of the common registry. Copies the component into the checkout at its exact digest, at stage alpha, for review, and prints what it copied.

title: stego registry inspect
description: <component> is the component name. It prints the component's name, version, namespace, the ports it provides and requires, its slots and its settings with their types and defaults, as text. --archetype names an archetype instead, and prints every input a declaration may give the archetype's active component set, as checking reads it: each component with its version, each setting with its type, allowed values, whether it is optional and its default, and each slot with its contract, as a table. With --json it prints only one JSON document, which holds the archetype and one row per input with every field. It exits non-zero and prints no row when the archetype is not in the registry, and names the archetypes the registry holds.

title: stego registry search
description: Each flag is a filter, and is optional: --provides a port the component provides, --requires a port it requires, --slot a slot it offers. Prints the components that match every filter given as a table, in name order: a header line, then one line per component, with its name, version, ports provided, ports required and slots in columns.

title: stego registry sunsets
description: Each <checkout> is a service checkout to read. Prints every recorded service that uses a component past its sunset without a dated acceptance, with the component and the date, and exits non-zero when there is any.

title: stego registry quality
description: Takes no flag. Prints each ga component's standing against the quality bar and the share of ga components that hold it, and exits non-zero when the share is below 100%.

title: stego registry fills
description: --slot is the slot and is required. --component names the component that owns the slot, and is required when more than one component of the active set declares a slot of that name. Prints each fill of the project that implements the slot, with who qualified it and when, or that there is none. Refuses a slot name that more than one component declares when --component is not given, and names each such component.

title: stego registry add
description: <component folder> holds the component's definition, its slot contracts and its generator, in the registry checkout. Checks the config schema, ports, slots, namespace, architecture role and outputs, and the provider import against the pinned runtime library version, and prints the component and its version as accepted. Exits non-zero, and names each fault with the component, file or version it concerns, when a check fails.

title: stego registry release
description: <component> is the component whose emitted code or slot contract changed. --version is its new version and is required. Records the new version and prints it. Exits non-zero, and names the reason, when the emitted code changed under the old version, or when a slot contract under the same slot name fails a breaking-change rule against the contract last released; it then names the slot and each rule.

title: stego registry compose
description: Takes no flag. Reads the registry sources that the project pins, composes them into one active set, and prints each source with its reference and the parts it adds. Exits non-zero, and names the part and both registries, when a local part would replace a common part; and names the source or input when a source is not pinned at a full commit, is not clean, or the composition is over its limits.

title: stego registry introduce
description: <component folder> holds the component with the outcome it serves, its best-in-field references or why none exists, and its promise list. --stage is alpha or beta, and --sunset is the date it stops working; both are required. Adds the component at that stage and prints it with its sunset. Exits non-zero, and names what is missing, when the date is past or the component states no outcome, no reference statement or no contract.

title: stego registry graduate
description: <component> is the component to move one stage up. Moves it from alpha to beta or from beta to ga; at ga it removes the sunset date and lets the component take over the port name it waited for. Prints the new stage. Exits non-zero, and names each missing piece of the quality bar, a stale or undecided reference comparison, or a port and the conformance suite not passed at the current digest, when the component cannot reach ga.

title: stego registry retire
description: <component> is a component that did not graduate or that reached its sunset. Removes it from the active registry and prints that it is retired.

title: stego registry curate
description: <archetype folder> holds the archetype's components, the default provider of each port, its default concerns and its smallest example content. Checks the archetype and prints it as accepted, with the provider of each port. Exits non-zero, and names the port, component or stage, when a component is not ga, a required port has no provider or more than one, a default provider is not ga, or a ga archetype lacks a default concern.

title: stego registry extend
description: <archetype> is the archetype to extend. --mixin is the folder of the mixin, with the components and slots it brings and the mixins it requires; it is required. Adds the mixin to the archetype and prints it with what it brings. Exits non-zero, and names the part, component or mixin, when the mixin replaces a part of the archetype, brings a component that is not ga, or lacks a mixin it requires.

title: stego registry define-port
description: <port folder> holds the port's name, what a provider undertakes to supply, the meaning of each field, and its conformance test suite. Records the port and prints it. Exits non-zero, and names the port or field, when the port name is already defined or a field has no meaning.

title: stego registry declare-slot
description: <component> is the component that offers the slot and <slot> the slot's name. --contract is the contract file that a fill implements, and is required. Declares the slot and prints it. Exits non-zero, and names the slot with the file, the component or each rule, when the contract file is missing or holds no service, no generator of the component uses the slot, or a changed contract under the same name fails a breaking-change rule.

title: stego registry evidence
description: <component> is the component. --kind is the kind of evidence and --file the evidence; both are required. A benchmark gives one figure per reference. Records the evidence at the component's current digest, or at its contract set's digest for a reference comparison, and prints it with each benchmark figure that regressed from the previous version. Exits non-zero, and names the reason, when the digest is not the current one or a benchmark has no figure per reference.

title: stego registry consumers
description: <component> is the component. Each <checkout> is a service checkout to read. Prints every recorded service that uses the component, with the version it pins. It writes nothing.
